lead.headline: Goyal says US already agreed India gets lower duties than rival countries
signal: The claim comes from the Indian side; the article gives no US confirmation or duty figures.
If the advantage holds, Indian exporters gain against rival suppliers, but the real rates are unknown until the text is signed.
lead.hook: Commerce minister Piyush Goyal says the US has agreed to give India ==preferential market access with lower import duties than competing countries==, though the first-phase trade deal is still unsigned.
points: Goyal said the understanding was reached between Modi and Trump when they announced a broad framework for the bilateral trade agreement (BTA) a few months ago.
India and the US finalised the framework for the deal's first phase in February.
Signing was expected earlier, but changes in the US tariff structure forced further negotiations, which are still underway.
An official recently said Washington assured New Delhi of a comparative tariff advantage for Indian goods.
lead.key_stat: First-phase BTA · unsigned since Feb framework
lead.editors_read: The tariff structure keeps shifting, so a 'lower than competitors' promise is only worth what the final rate table says. Watch whether the signed text names rates; a verbal assurance can be undone by the next US tariff change.
lead.evidence_of: India seeks tariff advantage as US trade rules shift

frontpage.headline: US floated Ukraine leaving Donbas in return for NATO membership, Zelensky says
signal: If Moscow keeps its NATO red line, the offer stalls; the article says Russia's position has not shifted.
Zelensky may be publicising the idea to reopen NATO as an option.
frontpage.hook: Zelensky says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from Donbas if it joined NATO, the ==first time the two have been== linked in talks; the US has not confirmed it.
points: A US official told the BBC many ideas are discussed but any deal needs both parties' agreement. Kushner urged confidentiality and said both sides know compromises are needed.
Zelensky says he would put a full package to a referendum if it had security guarantees, no limits on Ukraine's army and rebuilding funds.
Russia holds roughly a fifth of Ukraine and says no ceasefire until a final deal, including Ukraine ceding the rest of Donbas and Crimea.
The Kremlin has long called Ukrainian NATO membership a red line; other NATO members are also wary, and Ukraine reportedly sees it as unrealistic.
Europe is to get a seat at future talks, with a team of Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland plus EU officials.
frontpage.editors_read: The pitch tests how much Russia values Donbas against blocking NATO. Kushner's quick damping suggests Washington did not want it public. The likelier near-term outcome is more talks with Europe at the table, not a deal.
frontpage.evidence_of: Ukraine peace talks widen to Europe and NATO

frontpage.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns over relationship with suspected Chinese spy
signal: Chip export enforcement is now a CEO-level risk, not just a compliance issue.
If more executives face this scrutiny, expect tighter security vetting at AI firms.
frontpage.hook: Jensen Huang resigned after 33 years as CEO of the ==$4tn chip company==, following reports of a close relationship with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China; Nasdaq fell 4%.
points: The New York Times reported Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which the US is investigating for diverting AI chips to China. Reports of two more affairs with employees followed.
The relationship appears to have helped move billions of dollars of Nvidia chips to China, per the report. China calls the claims a smear.
Nvidia hired a law firm to investigate, Trump says the FBI will probe, Huang agreed to testify to Congress and faces a shareholder lawsuit.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under pressure over why Megaspeed was not blacklisted.
Experts say honeypot (romance-based) tactics are old and human error is the weakest link; security firms expect more demand.
frontpage.editors_read: The story links a governance failure to export policy: enforcement gaps around Megaspeed are now a political liability for Washington. Expect hawks to push tighter licensing, which feeds the rare earths risk reported separately today.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

frontpage.headline: Iran says it targeted US radar site in Bahrain with six drones
signal: The Strait of Hormuz is a key route for global energy supply, so prolonged closure keeps oil-price risk alive, including for import-dependent India.
frontpage.hook: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it targeted a US radar defence site at al-Riffa Air Base in Bahrain with six drones; no damage was claimed or detailed.
points: Bahrain's Interior Ministry had issued repeated threat warnings hours earlier, urging residents to seek shelter.
The IRGC said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and blamed Washington's 'failure' to escort ships through it.
It warned any US aggression would meet a harsher response.
The war began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran on Feb. 28, followed by an April ceasefire; fighting resumed as talks stalled despite a June memorandum of understanding.
frontpage.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

frontpage.headline: Brain implants turn ALS patients' signals directly into speech and singing
signal: Removing the text step lets users keep rhythm and emphasis, which brings the technology closer to everyday use.
frontpage.hook: UC Davis researchers decoded brain signals from a 46-year-old man with ALS into intelligible speech, and a 58-year-old former singer sang a musical scale using implants.
points: Earlier systems decoded signals into text first, then into computer-generated speech, causing a delay that made conversation hard.
In those systems, electrodes detected signals, software decoded phonemes, words appeared on screen, and the user clicked to trigger speech.
The new direct translation is to be presented next week at the Society for Neuroscience conference.
An outside expert, Cindy Chestek, called it the first system 'good enough' for real communication.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI-linked brain interfaces approach everyday use

frontpage.headline: ICJ to rule Thursday on whether Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
signal: A genocide finding would add pressure on Min Aung Hlaing and could push states to block arms and jet fuel supplies, though enforcement is weak.
frontpage.hook: The International Court of Justice rules Thursday on whether Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, after seven years of deliberation; it has never before found a state responsible for genocide.
points: The Gambia brought the case, alleging breach of the 1948 genocide convention; Myanmar denies genocide and says it targeted insurgents.
The hard issue is proving 'intent to destroy' a group; the Balkans cases found no state directly responsible, though Serbia failed to prevent Srebrenica.
Over 1 million Rohingya live in Bangladesh camps; fewer than 600,000 remain in Myanmar.
The ruling hints at how judges may treat South Africa's genocide case against Israel; US envoy Mike Waltz warned against a standard usable against 'allied soldiers'.
The court cannot enforce rulings; UN Security Council action is unlikely given US-China divisions.
frontpage.evidence_of: International law tested against powerful states

frontpage.headline: India's October goods exports hit record $49.47B, up 45%
signal: Petroleum is among the drivers, so part of the jump may reflect prices rather than volume; the article does not break this out.
A near-$40B monthly deficit shows imports still outpace exports.
frontpage.hook: India's goods exports rose 45% to ==$49.47 billion in October== from $34.11 billion a year earlier, while imports rose 16% to $89.35 billion.
points: The trade deficit widened to a year high of $39.88 billion.
CII's Budhia credited petroleum, electronics, engineering products and gems and jewellery.
He said non-petroleum exports also grew strongly, including chemicals and textiles.
CII credits free trade agreements and the Export Promotion Mission; it sees $1 trillion each in goods and services exports as achievable.
frontpage.evidence_of: India seeks tariff advantage as US trade rules shift

frontpage.headline: Indian stocks rebound 11% as AI trade unwinds
signal: India's recovery depends on global money leaving AI; if AI stocks recover, that flow could reverse.
frontpage.hook: The MSCI India gauge has rebounded 11% from an October six-month low, adding over ==$400 billion in value== and nearly erasing this year's losses as the AI trade unwinds.
points: Indian stocks fell in the first nine months as AI drew global capital elsewhere.
India's relative lack of AI exposure is now an advantage.
Global funds are also more positive on India's $5.4 trillion equity market as oil prices retreat and earnings growth accelerates.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI trade is losing political and market support

frontpage.headline: Stanford brain-activity score predicts Alzheimer's risk years before symptoms
signal: If brain activity can be shifted, early screening could target interventions before plaques form; that remains untested.
frontpage.hook: A Stanford brain-activity score, ARC, separated super agers from Alzheimer's patients with about 85% accuracy and predicted decline in 1,300+ healthy adults aged 55-70 for up to 12 years.
points: Researchers compared resting-state fMRI scans of 180 super agers (75+, memory like a 45-year-old) and 110 Alzheimer's patients.
People whose scores looked more Alzheimer's-like were likelier to decline, build amyloid plaques and be diagnosed; most follow-up lasted five to six years.
The authors say ARC predicted decline as well as or better than amyloid, tau and genetic markers, and improved when combined with them.
ARC is not a diagnosis. It is unknown whether changing brain activity would alter the disease; a trial will test cognitive training.
frontpage.evidence_of: Science finds earlier signals of brain disease

stories.headline: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first
signal: If junior roles keep shrinking, firms may face a shortage of experienced staff later.
Evidence is mixed: macro factors may explain part of the drop.
stories.hook: An RBA analysis finds AI has barely displaced jobs in Australia, but young workers entering exposed fields like software and customer service fare worse.
points: Job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, steepest in the highest-exposure group.
In that group, workers aged 15-24 and young graduates have weaker employment and higher unemployment than older workers.
The study does not prove causation and measures theoretical exposure, not actual company use; business cycle and remote work shifts could also matter.
Stanford found 22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs down 13% in relative employment; Anthropic's junior technical hires fell from 27% to 9% since early 2025, though it calls itself a special case.
A Denmark study of 25,000 workers found no wage or hours change, and a Pittsburgh study says problems began months before ChatGPT.
stories.evidence_of: AI hits entry-level jobs first

stories.headline: Runway open-sources Praxis-1, a video-trained robot controller
signal: If video pretraining cuts the robot data needed, entry costs for robotics fall; Runway says that is still unproven.
stories.hook: Runway released Praxis-1, a robot control model, with open weights and code under the Apache 2.0 licence, which allows commercial use.
points: It takes camera images, text instructions and robot position, predicts how a scene will change, and computes movements.
On Nvidia's RoboLab-120 it scores 46.2%, versus 42.9% for FLUX 3 Action; it ranks fifth overall. Runway ran all tests itself.
On a real Franka arm it succeeded 88 of 100 attempts versus 80 for FLUX 3 Action. On an unseen robot, after 95 hours of data, it hit 80% in simulation versus 52.4% for Google's RT-1.
It still needs robot-specific data, confuses similar objects and cannot plan long tasks. The standard version needs an 80 GB GPU.
stories.evidence_of: General-purpose AI models are moving into robot control

stories.headline: OpenAI folds robotics researchers into other teams
signal: If general models keep closing the gap, standalone robot-AI startups face pressure; real-world tests are still thin.
stories.hook: OpenAI reorganised its robotics team, moving researchers under Mark Chen's research team and hardware staff under Greg Brockman's Applied organisation, and says robotics work continues.
points: Fortune reports the decision came so fast that OpenAI's booth at the Conference on Robot Learning sat empty.
OpenAI apparently believes general models like GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly.
In an Nvidia study, an Astra agent hit 74.8% on simulated tasks versus 51% for the best specialised models.
On StationeryBench, Astra fully completed 7 of 100 tasks; Ai2's MolmoAct2 completed none.
Specialised models may still win on cost, reliability, speed and energy use. Altman reportedly targets a first public robot demo in 2027.
stories.evidence_of: General-purpose AI models are moving into robot control

stories.headline: How deeply India's AI build-out depends on Nvidia
signal: Huang's exit is unlikely to change software lock-in, but export-rule shifts could slow Indian GPU supply.
Alternatives such as TPUs and AMD are closest to ready for inference workloads.
stories.hook: Of 44,077 compute units empanelled on the IndiaAI portal, 35,985 are Nvidia, while Counterpoint cites $4-5 billion committed to Nvidia-powered data centres in India.
points: Yotta plans 20,000+ Blackwell Ultra GPUs, AMI has ordered 29,000 Rubin GPUs, and L&T Vyoma is building a 10,000-GPU facility.
IndiaAI had onboarded over 45,000 GPUs by June and approved 237 projects for subsidised compute by August.
CUDA, Nvidia's software layer, creates switching costs: moving to AMD can mean rewriting software.
US licensing is tightening on seven countries; India is not named, but experts say favourable treatment is no supply guarantee.
Nvidia backs 4,000+ Indian startups and invested in Sarvam AI's $74M tranche; an expert says reducing dependence could take half a decade.
stories.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

also.line: South Korea's top tax accountant exam scorer (397.5/400) admitted cheating with a microcamera and generative AI; the college entrance exam is Thursday, and the government is preparing countermeasures.

stories.headline: Sebi to issue AI guidelines for capital markets
signal: Regulated firms using AI in trading or advice will need disclosure and human sign-off processes.
A better listing route could ease early public-market access for long-gestation startups.
stories.hook: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey says the regulator will soon issue guidelines on AI in capital markets, centred on disclosures, accountability and 'human-in-the-loop' oversight.
points: The guidelines build on a June 2025 consultation paper on responsible AI/ML use in securities markets.
Sebi is also reviewing its framework so AI use does not weaken investor protection or market integrity.
It is taking stock of cryptographic systems, as quantum __risks are expected to sharpen around 2032-35__.
A working group is studying how to make the Innovators Growth Platform more attractive to deep-tech and biotech startups, as the platform has not gained traction.
stories.evidence_of: India is tightening rules on AI use

stories.headline: Zetwerk revenue up 18.3% to Rs 4,599 crore, but loss widens
signal: Growing orders suggest revenue visibility, but costs are rising faster than revenue growth, so profitability is the open question.
stories.hook: Zetwerk's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.3% to Rs 4,599 crore from Rs 3,889 crore, while its net loss widened 43.1% to Rs 88 crore.
points: Manufacturing contributed Rs 2,546.5 crore, up 14.9%; the ecosystem business grew 22.8% to Rs 2,053 crore.
Employee costs rose 51.8% and finance costs 32.4%; total expenses rose 19.6% to Rs 4,689 crore.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 69% to Rs 274 crore, per the company.
Order wins were Rs 4,613 crore, up 44%, and the manufacturing order book grew 67%; the order book converts into revenue over about two years.
It listed on October 23 at Rs 159.25, a 5.5% premium to the Rs 151 issue price.
stories.evidence_of: Indian startups turn to public markets

stories.headline: ==First Tejas Mk1A may reach== IAF as early as January
signal: The source is anonymous. If the January date holds, the 180 aircraft on order begin to flow; engine supply remains the key dependency.
stories.source: Defence BREAKING NEWS | Defence LATEST NEWS | Defence NEWS TODAY | Defence LIVE UPDATES | Defence TRENDING NEWS | – ThePrint
stories.hook: The first Tejas Mk1A is likely to be handed to the Indian Air Force early in 2027, possibly in January, nearly three years after the original February 2024 deadline.
points: HAL's contract for 83 jets was signed in February 2021 for Rs 36,400 crore.
Delays were mainly due to late F404-IN20 engines from GE Aerospace, plus weapons and systems integration.
Deliveries of the first tranche were originally due to finish by February 2028.
A follow-on order for 97 aircraft, worth over Rs 62,370 crore, came in September 2025, with deliveries starting FY 2027-28 over six years.
stories.evidence_of: India builds defence capacity but is slowed by imported parts

stories.headline: Ukrainian drone maker UFORCE ==raises $700M== at $6B valuation
signal: Investors are paying for battlefield-tested products; if wars keep proving cheap drones, crewed platforms lose budget share.
stories.hook: UFORCE, a Ukrainian maker of aerial, naval and land drones, raised $700 million at a $6 billion valuation, up from about $1 billion in March.
points: The round was co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK's National Wealth Fund.
The CEO says bookings more than doubled in a year from a base of several hundred million dollars, without giving figures.
The company says its NEMESIS drones have flown over 300,000 combat flights and its MAGURA vessels helped destroy more than a dozen Russian warships.
Allied-country defence startups raised $27.1 billion through September, nearly double all of 2025.
It will expand manufacturing in Ukraine and allied countries; the CEO says Ukraine's needs come first.
stories.evidence_of: Capital and armies are shifting to cheap autonomous weapons

also.line: Bengaluru's Astrobase Space Technologies will invest Rs 800 crore to add 339 acres to its 22-acre rocket testing site at Thimmasamudram, Andhra Pradesh, for stage development and hot-fire tests.

stories.headline: China could tighten rare earths if US escalates chip curbs over Nvidia
signal: Rare earths remain China's main counter to chip curbs; if the US tightens, expect a swap of restrictions, hitting manufacturers dependent on both.
stories.hook: Chinese analysts say Beijing could tighten rare earths exports if Washington restricts chip sales further after the Huang scandal, though broader trade talks are expected to stay on track.
points: Victor Gao says US politicians exploiting the scandal would 'force China to tighten control of rare earths exports'.
The EIU's Xu Tianchen also expects tighter rare earth curbs if the US tightens chip controls.
Wang Yingliang says China's chip inventories and growing domestic capability cushion short-term impact, and he expects current US export policy to hold barring escalation.
Xi and Trump are expected to meet at the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week, with tariffs, farm purchases and rare earths on the table.
stories.evidence_of: AI chips are now a national security fight

also.line: China's first fully AI-generated feature film, made with no human actors or camera crew, flopped at the box office.

stories.headline: India lifted 500M out of poverty, but many remain one shock away
signal: Headline poverty cuts can coexist with fragile household finances; healthcare and price shocks are the main risks.
stories.source: Al Jazeera – Breaking News, World News and Video from Al Jazeera
stories.hook: The World Bank says India lifted nearly 500 million people out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, cutting extreme poverty from 27.1% to 2.6%, but many remain barely above the line.
points: India has not published an official consumption-based poverty estimate in over a decade, so the World Bank provides the numbers.
The line for a family of three is about Rs 7,380 a month; one family spending Rs 11,000 still goes hungry by month-end.
Consumer prices rose at least 51% from September 2016 to September 2025, and wages have not kept pace.
Free or subsidised grain reaches nearly 800 million people; the top 1% own 40% of wealth.
Economist Santosh Mehrotra says the line is too low and ignores rural-urban differences; one shock like illness can push families back.
stories.evidence_of: Headline growth hides household fragility

stories.headline: India pushes to rewrite its ASEAN trade deal
signal: Stronger rules of origin could stop third-country goods using preferential routes; success depends on market access in Indonesia and Vietnam.
stories.hook: India ran a ==$51.55 billion trade deficit== with ASEAN in 2025-26 ($89.96B imports against $38.41B exports) and wants the AITIGA trade deal reviewed this financial year.
points: Total trade was $128.38 billion; India says the 2009 goods agreement has not delivered for its exporters.
The review, begun in 2022, covers tariffs, non-tariff barriers, rules of origin and customs procedures.
The Jakarta committee meeting in October agreed to speed up outstanding chapters; the next meets in India in January 2027.
Malaysia is negotiating an upgrade of its India pact and the Philippines wants a preferential trade agreement, but India wants AITIGA done first.
Modi's Manila visit also covers maritime security and digital public infrastructure.
stories.evidence_of: India seeks tariff advantage as US trade rules shift

stories.headline: Student protests in India and France target broken education promise
signal: When exams and schools look unfair, tolerance for inequality falls; recurring leaks raise political cost for governments.
stories.hook: Large student protests in India and France this fall are driven by a shared anger that education no longer reliably delivers advancement.
points: In India, protests followed the cancellation of a medical admissions exam after questions leaked online; students had to retake it.
In France, protests began over decrepit schools, opaque university admissions and absent teachers, and spread to rioting in some cities.
NYT calls the underlying issue a broken 'meritocratic bargain': education is open, rewards merit and so justifies hierarchy.
Princeton's Nicholas Kuipers notes all selection systems create losers, and the question is who.
stories.evidence_of: AI hits entry-level jobs first

stories.headline: Microfinance lenders branch into MSME and gold loans after RBI eases rule
signal: Lower concentration should reduce risk, but MFIs move into crowded segments where established lenders hold the advantage.
stories.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
stories.hook: Since the RBI cut the minimum share of qualifying microfinance assets from 75% to ==60% of portfolios==, lenders are moving into MSME, property, vehicle and gold loans.
points: The change followed stress and rising delinquencies from heavy exposure to one borrower segment.
Fusion Finance raised MSME ticket sizes from Rs 5-15 lakh to up to Rs 50 lakh and __aims to lift non-microfinance assets from about 14%__ to 30-35% in two years.
Aarohan, at 68% microfinance, will pick one of four new lines: property, home improvement, vehicle or gold loans.
Executives expect gradual change given competition and the cost of building products, talent and distribution.
stories.evidence_of: Indian lenders diversify after microfinance stress

stories.headline: Private equity is funding India's aerospace suppliers
signal: The targets are industry goals, not forecasts; success depends on firms winning design and IP content, not just assembly.
stories.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
stories.hook: India's aerospace manufacturing industry is expected to grow from about ==$2 billion== to $20 billion over the next decade, with private equity now available to fund it.
points: Airbus and Boeing are seeking more suppliers in countries like India.
The industry wants India's share of the global aerospace supply chain raised from 1-2% to 10%.
The Aerospace India Association's director general says private capital is the big difference from the 2004-08 wave, when firms could not scale.
Firms aim to move from build-to-print work to own designs such as motors and actuators.
AeroConnect 2026, the association's inaugural conference, is on 19 November in Bengaluru.
stories.evidence_of: Capital is flowing into India's hard-tech manufacturing

also.line: Bitcoin fell below $65,000 on Sunday to $64,962, its lowest since July, as investors favoured AI stocks and priced a likely Fed rate hike.

stories.headline: India approves 1,150-kV corridor to move solar power east
signal: If green hydrogen demand lags, the line may be underused; its value depends on industry arriving in the east.
stories.hook: India's national transmission panel approved a 1,150-kV corridor linking western and eastern regions, estimated at Rs 68,800 crore and about six years to build.
points: It would be India's highest-voltage system, above the existing 765-kV, cutting losses because less current carries the same power.
Phase one links Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal, and connects to a 6,000 MW HVDC line carrying Bhadla solar power to Raigarh.
The full corridor spans about 3,750 circuit-km.
It targets Odisha's green hydrogen, ammonia, steel and EV hubs; planners considered 12 GW of demand but modelled loading at 3-3.5 GW.
GRID-INDIA and GETCO flag that the projected green hydrogen load remains uncertain.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: India's road-fuel demand to keep rising until 2034 despite EVs
signal: India remains a source of oil demand growth for years, keeping import and price exposure.
stories.hook: BloombergNEF projects India's road-fuel demand will peak at over 2.5 million barrels a day in 2034, even as EV adoption accelerates.
points: Growth comes from a larger vehicle fleet and heavier commercial transport use.
Electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers and cars eventually outweigh commercial growth and lower demand.
EV sales exceeded 2.4 million units last year, but apart from three-wheelers no segment is on track for 2030 electrification targets.
About $29 billion in charging infrastructure is needed by 2040.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

stories.headline: Indian solar manufacturing faces oversupply and consolidation
signal: Firms with upstream integration and strong balance sheets are likelier to survive a price war.
stories.hook: India has about ==225 GW of solar module== capacity against 40-45 GW of annual installations, and GREW Solar's Hiten Parekh expects consolidation to 20-25 major manufacturers.
points: Parekh expects aggressive pricing over the next two to three quarters as makers compete for orders.
Cell capacity is only about 38 GW; cell prices rose at least 1.5 times in six months and some raw materials about 2.5 times since February.
Regulatory uncertainty over ALMM List II after December complicates procurement; developers are locking in contracts six to eight months ahead.
US trade barriers constrain direct module exports, and possible Chinese equipment export curbs could delay new lines.
GREW plans 9 GW of cell capacity and an 8 GW wafer facility in Madhya Pradesh for 2027-28.
stories.evidence_of: India is building energy security through storage and local manufacturing

also.line: An IEA report says renewable expansion helped India avoid more than $100 billion (about Rs 9.4 lakh crore) in fuel imports since 2011.

stories.headline: Trump's pharma tariffs threaten India's generics model
signal: The conflict between reshoring and affordability may soften or delay tariffs; commodity-generic makers are most at risk.
stories.hook: Indian pharma exports to the US fell nearly 10% to ==$9.47 billion in FY26==, and proposed US tariffs on generics could squeeze the business further.
points: For some big Indian drugmakers the US brings 30-50% of revenue; Pharmexcil blames price erosion, a high base and inventory corrections for the fall.
Unbranded generics are 90% of US prescription volume, and US consumers pay 67 cents per dollar paid abroad for them.
Analysts see Lupin, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Granules and Glenmark as more exposed; Sun, Cipla, Zydus and Torrent as better placed. Cipla makes 35-40% of its US sales locally.
Newly elected Democrats campaigned on cheaper healthcare, which clashes with tariffs that would raise generic prices.
stories.evidence_of: US tariffs reshape India's export sectors

stories.headline: Synchron pauses trials of second-generation brain implant
signal: Component and regulatory delays can slow hardware startups even when the science works.
stories.hook: Synchron, a leading brain-computer interface startup, paused clinical trials of its second-generation wireless device and will cut jobs in New York; it says the pause is not safety related.
points: Its first-generation device threads a catheter through veins to place a stent near the motor cortex.
CEO Tom Oxley said a delayed component slowed its FDA submission.
The company is developing a new device, per WIRED.
It is the first major setback for one of the field's leaders, alongside Neuralink and Precision Neuroscience.
stories.evidence_of: AI-linked brain interfaces approach everyday use

stories.headline: Earth's own atmosphere may have worsened May 2024 solar storm
signal: Forecast models may need to include atmospheric ion outflow; storms disrupt satellites, GPS and power grids.
stories.hook: About ==85% of ions in Earth's== ring current during the May 2024 superstorm came from its own upper atmosphere, not the solar wind, per Japan's Arase satellite.
points: The storm pushed the SYM-H disturbance index to −518 nanotesla, the second-largest since 1981.
Arase measured a 40% drop in magnetic field intensity about 16,000 km above Earth, closer to the planet than similar drops seen before.
Heavy oxygen ions from Earth may have strengthened the disturbance.
Current forecasts rely mainly on solar wind conditions.
Researchers back a proposed JAXA two-satellite mission, FACTORS.
stories.evidence_of: Science finds new drivers of familiar hazards

also.line: Chemical signatures in fossilised teeth suggest dinosaurs may have eaten seaweed and other ocean foods more than 100 million years ago (summary from limited source text).
